messages:
support-bot: escalation from CS — tenant corpX reporting p95/p99 spike for /v1/generate since this morning's runtime rollout (deploy-2026-03-17). link: https://dash.internal/reports/tenant/corpX
alex: seeing the alert, thanks. can someone paste the canary id and runtime version? :eyes:
maria: canary id: canary-2026-03-17-9, runtime-version: rtv-2.14.0 -> rolled to 2.15.0 for canary then gradual rollout started at 08:30 PT
tj: I already eyeballed telemetry — p50 stable, p95 jumped ~300ms, p99 up ~1.6s for corpX routes. pattern aligns with requests that hit auth refresh path (~token refresh).
samir: copying traces — some long tail RPCs to auth-service at ~450-600ms which then block request processing. attaching a sample trace id: trace-0a1b2c (see logs).
alex: hmm. rtv-2.15.0 included kernel scheduler change (scheduler=v2) and a small change to sidecar auth retry behavior. which one rolled into canary?
maria: both. scheduler change: switched to 'batch-priority' kernel selector for slower segments to improve throughput. small auth change: changed sync auth cache miss to a non-blocking async fetch but with a short sync fallback (100ms).
jen: customer says they ramped traffic to 60 tps after the rollout. corpX has a lot of short requests (few tokens) — that's a classic throughput/latency tradeoff.
alex: can someone run a quick logs query: p95 grouped by model + kernel_selector for corpX from 08:00-09:30? use observability query:
```
SELECT
  model, kernel_selector, quant, percentile(latency_ms,95) as p95
FROM requests
WHERE tenant = 'corpX' AND ts BETWEEN 2026-03-17T08:00:00Z AND 2026-03-17T09:30:00Z
GROUP BY model, kernel_selector, quant
ORDER BY p95 DESC
```
tj: posted results — majority of high-p95 rows are kernel_selector=batch-priority + quant=int8 on model-embedder-v3
samir: digging into node-level metrics — hosts with scheduler=v2 show higher queue depth in hotpath queues and increased time_waiting_for_kv_cache (seen in sidecar metrics).
ops-oncall: at a high level, do we have a fast mitigation? rollback the scheduler change for corpX traffic or reduce canary traffic?
alex: two options: 1) patch canary flag to route corpX back to scheduler=v1 (config override), or 2) full rollback of kernel change from rtv-2.15.0 to rtv-2.14.0 for all rollout. I prefer targeted rollback to minimize blast radius.
maria: we have a per-tenant routing override feature — I can flip corpX to use scheduler=v1 for the next 30m. should relieve tail while we bisect.
jen: flipping now would be best. corpX is in active escalation with CS.
deploy-bot: starting config change: set route.override.corpX.kernel_selector = v1 (change-id: cfg-9876). deploying to control-plane...
support-bot: notif sent to CS that we're applying a targeted rollback for corpX routes.
(deploy-bot): change applied in 12s.
ops-oncall: after toggle, p99 dropped ~1.2s within two minutes on corpX, p95 back to expected values. :thumbsup:
alex: great. we need to root cause — it's not enough to flip config. let's bisect which part of rtv-2.15.0 caused the queueing. candidates: kernel scheduler v2, async auth fallback tweak, or the quantization kernel change that adjusted batch boundaries.
tj: I'll run a canary-bisect job that deploys sub-variants: (A) scheduler=v2 + old auth, (B) scheduler=v1 + new auth, (C) scheduler=v2 + new auth + old quant kernels. will run with traffic mirror of corpX (synthetic bench) to reproduce tail.
samir: repro steps for bench:
```
# mirror 100% of corpX requests for 5m into test cluster
curl -X POST https://mirror.internal/traffic -d '{"tenant":"corpX","duration":300}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer mirror-token'
# run telemetry collection
kusto run query "SELECT percentile(latency_ms,99) FROM test_requests WHERE tenant='corpX'"
```
jen: timeline for bisect? we need quick answers to report to customer.
tj: start now — expected ~20m for a single variant run. I'll parallelize two variants. posting CI job id: bisect-2244.
alex: also capture auth-service timings. if auth refresh requests are synchronous in kernel v2 for certain paths, that could explain blocking behavior. add instrumentation: sidecar.auth.latency.breakdown by cache_hit/miss.
ops-oncall: also add a temporary circuit-breaker for auth backend calls to fail-fast after 200ms — reduces queueing pressure if backend slow.
maria: created ticket INF-4582 to follow up on permanent fixes: (1) revert kernel selector change until we can tune batching heuristics, (2) make auth fetch fully async without fallback, (3) add rate-limited fallback cache for token refreshes.
(deploy-bot): bisect jobs started: bisect-2244-A, bisect-2244-B (parallel).
tj: early results after 12m: variant B (scheduler=v1 + new auth) shows p99 stable; variant A (scheduler=v2 + old auth) shows elevated p99. looks like scheduler=v2 is main suspect.
samir: confirmed — node queue_depth metrics correlate with scheduler=v2 hosts. kernel v2 increases inter-batch wait for short-request-heavy tenants causing head-of-line blocking when auth misses happen.
alex: OK. mitigation plan: keep corpX routed to scheduler=v1 until full rollback of scheduler change in next patch. we should throttle scheduler=v2 rollout and add additional batching heuristics for short request workloads.
jen: informing CS and account team. sending note: "We applied a targeted routing rollback which restored latency. We're bisecting and will revert the scheduler globally if needed."
support-bot: CS updated tenant corpX and scheduled a follow-up call.
ops-oncall: follow-up actions (short):
- immediate: leave corpX on scheduler=v1, enable auth circuit-breaker 200ms (ops runbook), alert if p99 > baseline
- short-term: roll rtv-2.15.0 change for scheduler-> rtv-2.14.1 (rollback) if further tenants affected
- medium-term: tune batch-priority heuristics + add per-tenant short-request override
- long-term: add e2e canary that mirrors short-request tenants during kernel changes

alex: adding owners: tj (bisect & batch tuning), samir (metric dashboards + runbook), maria (config + patch), jen (customer comms). I'll create PR for rollback checklist.
maria: PR created: https://repo.internal/infra/pull/1420 — rollback playbook + telemetry checks.
alex: thanks everyone. keep updates in this thread. after rollback PR merges we'll schedule a postmortem and add an eval to catch similar regressions. :white_check_mark:
